changes.before: Events A and B are mutually exclusive: they cannot occur together. Their probabilities are P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.2. Are they independent?
changes.after: Events A and B are mutually exclusive: they cannot occur together. Their probabilities are P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.2. Which answer correctly states whether they are independent and explains why?

changes.before: In a fictional supply model, workshop A makes 60% of the sensors and workshop B makes 40%. A sensor from A is defective with probability 2%; one from B is defective with probability 6%. A sensor is selected at random from the combined supply. Given that it is defective, what is the probability it came from B?
changes.after: In a fictional supply model, workshop A makes 60% of the sensors and workshop B makes 40%. A sensor from A is defective with probability 2%; one from B is defective with probability 6%. A sensor is selected uniformly at random from the combined supply. Given that it is defective, what is the probability it came from B?

changes.before: A fictional checker flags 90% of defective files and 10% of nondefective files. Compare two collections where the defective share is 1% and 10%, respectively. The checker's conditional flagging rates stay the same. How does P(defective given flagged) change as the defective share rises?
changes.after: A fictional checker flags 90% of defective files and 10% of nondefective files. Compare two collections where the defective share is 1% and 10%, respectively. A file is selected uniformly at random from each collection. The checker's conditional flagging rates stay the same. How does P(defective given flagged) change as the defective share rises?
